chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Any man who enters into a sale transaction has the option (to cancel) until they part company; when they part company, the sale becomes binding."

He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "My father bought a piece of land called al-Uraidh from a man, purchasing it from its owner for dinars. He said, 'I will give you silver (dirhams) for every dinar, ten dirhams.' So he sold it to him for that. My father stood up quickly, and I followed him. I said, 'O father, why did you stand up quickly?' He said, 'I wanted the sale to become binding.'"
ai.seo_question: What is the rule regarding the cancellation of a sale before parties separate?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* codifies the principle of *khiyar al-majlis*, granting parties the right to rescind a contract until they physically separate, a rule derived from the Prophet’s practice and affirmed by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). The narrative of the Imam’s swift departure after purchasing the land of 'Al-Uraidh' serves as a practical demonstration of how to intentionally finalize a sale, highlighting the juristic importance of the 'separation' (*iftirāq*) as the moment of binding obligation.
